content.title: About
content.content: A decaffeinated carbonated soft drink with a pepper flavor is a non‑alcoholic beverage in which caffeine has been removed and the aroma comes from black‑pepper extract. The drink offers a mild spiciness, refreshing taste and characteristic fizz. It is marketed as an original alternative to traditional colas and energy drinks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepper‑flavored soft drinks first appeared in the early 2000s as a niche experiment.
Caffeine is removed using supercritical CO₂ extraction, preserving the original flavor profile.
Black pepper in small doses enhances the perception of sweetness, making the drink taste less sugary than regular colas.
The beverage is often served in Asian‑cuisine restaurants where its spiciness pairs with classic dishes.
In some countries the product is classified as a “special drink” and must be labeled for pepper content.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Black‑pepper extract contains piperine, which may stimulate gastric secretions and aid digestion.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Pepper is rich in antioxidants that help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Caffeine‑free
items.content: The lack of caffeine makes the drink safe for caffeine‑sensitive individuals and suitable for evening consumption.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Piperine can slightly increase metabolic rate, contributing to more efficient calorie burning.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any carbonated beverage, it contributes to fluid intake when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Spiciness and irritation
items.content: The pepper flavor may cause a burning sensation in the mouth and stomach for people with high sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Pepper allergy
items.content: Rarely, people may experience an allergic reaction to pepper components.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Excessive consumption of carbonated drinks can lead to bloating and stomach discomfort.

items.title: Sugar and sweeteners
items.content: If the drink is sweetened, consider the amount of sugar or artificial sweeteners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled, preferably over ice. It pairs well with spicy snacks, sushi, chicken wings, and Asian dishes. It can also be used as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.
